## Overview & Epidemiology

- **Global Burden**: 5th most frequently diagnosed cancer & 5th leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide
- **Histology**: >95% adenocarcinomas
  - *Anatomic*: Cardia/proximal vs. non-cardia/distal
  - *Lauren Classification*: Intestinal (mass-forming, environmental/dietary) vs. Diffuse (discohesive, heritable)
- **Risk Factors**: *H. pylori* infection, smoking, high salt intake, obesity, hereditary syndromes (CDH1, Lynch, FAP, Juvenile Polyposis)
- **Prognosis**: Often diagnosed at advanced stage; early detection (screening programs) significantly improves survival

## AJCC TNM Staging (8th Edition)

- **Clinical (cTNM)**, **Pathologic (pTNM)**, **Post-neoadjuvant (ypTNM)**
- **Primary Tumor (T)**:
  - Tis/T1a: Mucosa | T1b: Submucosa | T2: Muscularis propria
  - T3: Subserosa | T4a: Serosa | T4b: Adjacent structures
- **Regional Nodes (N)**:
  - N0 | N1 (1–2) | N2 (3–6) | N3a (7–15) | N3b (≥16)
- **Distant Metastasis (M)**: M0 | M1
- **EGJ Tumors**: Epicenter >2 cm into proximal stomach → staged as gastric carcinoma

## Initial Workup & Evaluation (GAST-1)

- **Imaging & Endoscopy**:
  - H&P, CBC, comprehensive chemistry profile
  - EGD + multiple biopsies (6–8)
  - CT chest/abdomen/pelvis with oral & IV contrast
  - FDG-PET/CT (locally advanced/metastatic)
  - EUS (preferred for early vs. locally advanced staging)
- **Biomarker Testing (Universal/Newly Diagnosed)**:
  - MSI (PCR/NGS) or MMR (IHC)
  - PD-L1 (IHC, CPS)
  - HER2 & CLDN18.2 (if advanced/metastatic suspected)
  - Consider NGS
- **Additional**: Nutritional assessment, smoking cessation, family history screening, *H. pylori* testing/eradication, distress screening, Siewert classification

## Multidisciplinary Review & Primary Pathways (GAST-2)

- **Localized (cTis/cT1a)**: Endoscopic resection (ER) or surgery
- **Locoregional (cT1b–cT4a, cM0)**:
  - *Medically fit, resectable*: Surgery ± perioperative systemic therapy
  - *Medically fit, unresectable*: Chemoradiation or systemic therapy
  - *Nonsurgical candidate*: ER (early) or palliative management
- **Metastatic (cM1)**: Palliative management/best supportive care
- **Staging Laparoscopy**: Recommended for cT1b+ to evaluate peritoneal spread; cytology+ = pM1

## Response Assessment & Additional Management (GAST-3)

- **Post-Perioperative Therapy Restaging**:
  - CT chest/abdomen/pelvis ± FDG-PET/CT
  - EGD + biopsy (if neoadjuvant ICI used for MSI-H/dMMR)
- **Management Based on Response**:
  - *Resectable*: Proceed to surgery (preferred)
  - *Persistent local disease*: Surgery or palliative management
  - *New metastatic/unresectable*: Palliative management
- **MSI-H/dMMR with Complete Clinical Response**: Multidisciplinary decision for observation vs. surgery

## Postoperative Management: No Prior Systemic Therapy (GAST-4)

- **R0 Resection**:
  - `pTis / pT1a / superficial pT1b (≤500 μm), N0` → Observation
  - `Deep pT1b (>500 μm) or pT2, N0` → Observation or fluoropyrimidine-based chemoradiation (if high-risk features)
  - `pT3–pT4 or Any N+` → 
    - `< D2 dissection`: Fluoropyrimidine → chemoradiation → fluoropyrimidine **(Category 1)**
    - `D2 dissection`: Postoperative chemotherapy **(Category 1)**
- **R1/R2 Resection**: Fluoropyrimidine-based chemoradiation or palliative management

## Postoperative Management: Prior Systemic Therapy (GAST-5)

- **R0 Resection**: Continue systemic therapy **(Category 1)**
- **R1 Resection**: Chemoradiation (fluoropyrimidine-based) or consider re-resection
- **R2 Resection**: Chemoradiation or palliative management
- **ypM1 Disease**: Palliative management
- Follow all patients per surveillance guidelines (GAST-7)

## Principles of Endoscopic Staging & Therapy (GAST-A)

- **Diagnosis**: Map tumor location; take 6–8 biopsies; larger forceps improve yield
- **Staging**: EUS assesses T/N depth; FNA for suspicious nodes/ascites
- **Early-Stage Therapy (EMR/ESD)**:
  - Curative features: ≤2 cm, well/moderately differentiated, ≤500 μm invasion, no LVI, clear margins
  - Expanded criteria per Japanese/US guidelines
  - Unfavorable histology/deep invasion/LVI → Gastrectomy + lymphadenectomy
- **Palliative Endoscopy**: SEMS for obstruction, ablation for bleeding, feeding tubes for nutrition

## Principles of Pathologic Review & Biomarker Testing (GAST-B)

- **Pathology Report**: Invasion depth, histologic type, grade, margins, LVI, lymph nodes recovered (goal ≥16)
- **Treatment Response Scoring**: 0 (Complete) → 3 (Poor/No response)
- **HER2**: IHC 3+ or 2+/ISH+ → Trastuzumab eligible
- **CLDN18.2**: ≥75% viable cells with moderate/strong membrane staining → Zolbetuximab eligible
- **MSI/MMR**: Universal testing; refer positive cases to genetics
- **PD-L1**: Universal testing; CPS ≥1 positive; TAP score highly concordant & interchangeable
- **ctDNA/Liquid Biopsy**: Consider when tissue limited or biopsy unsafe

## Principles of Surgery (GAST-C)

- **Goal**: R0 resection with negative margins
- **Resection Types**: Distal, subtotal, or total gastrectomy based on location
- **Lymphadenectomy**:
  - D1: Perigastric nodes
  - D2: D1 + celiac axis nodes (left gastric, common hepatic, splenic arteries)
  - Goal: Examine ≥16 nodes
- **Minimally Invasive**: Considered in experienced centers; not recommended for T4b or bulky N2
- **Palliative**: Gastrojejunostomy, SEMS, venting/feeding tubes; lymph node dissection not required

## Principles of Radiation Therapy (GAST-G)

- **Planning**: Multidisciplinary review, CT simulation, IMRT/3D-CRT preferred
- **Target Volumes**: Tumor bed, anastomosis, location-specific nodal basins
- **Dose**: 45–50.4 Gy in 1.8 Gy daily fractions; boost possible for positive margins
- **Organ Constraints**: Strict limits for lungs, heart, liver, kidneys, bowel, spinal cord
- **Supportive Care**: Weekly monitoring, prophylactic antiemetics, nutrition support (<1500 kcal/day → enteral/IV)
- **Preoperative RT**: Not routinely recommended for resectable gastric cancer

## Combined Modality & Perioperative Therapy (GAST-F)

- **Perioperative Systemic Therapy**: Category 1 for resectable ≥cT2
- **Preferred Regimens**:
  - FLOT **(Category 1)**
  - FLOT + durvalumab: 
    - PD-L1 CPS≥1 or TAP≥1% **(Cat 1)**
    - cN0, PD-L1<1, or diffuse type **(Cat 2B)**
- **Postoperative Therapy**:
  - `< D2 dissection`: Chemoradiation (fluoropyrimidine-based)
  - `D2 dissection`: Chemotherapy (capecitabine/oxaliplatin or FOLFOX) **(Cat 1)**
- **Neoadjuvant ICI (MSI-H/dMMR)**: Nivo+ipi→nivo, pembrolizumab, dostarlimab, tremelimumab+durvalumab **(Cat 2A)**

## First-Line Systemic Therapy: Advanced/Metastatic

- **HER2-Positive**:
  - Fluoropyrimidine + oxaliplatin/cisplatin + trastuzumab ± pembrolizumab (if PD-L1 CPS≥1)
- **HER2-Negative**:
  - PD-L1 CPS≥1: Add ICI (nivolumab, pembrolizumab, tislelizumab) to fluoropyrimidine/platinum
  - CLDN18.2-Positive: Add zolbetuximab to fluoropyrimidine + oxaliplatin
- **MSI-H/dMMR (Any PD-L1)**: Pembrolizumab, dostarlimab, nivo+ipi, or chemo+ICI
- **General**: Oxaliplatin preferred over cisplatin; 2-drug regimens preferred for lower toxicity

## Second-Line & Subsequent Therapy

- **Preferred (Category 1)**:
  - Ramucirumab + paclitaxel
  - Docetaxel, paclitaxel, irinotecan, FOLFIRI
  - Trifluridine/tipiracil (3rd line+)
- **HER2-Positive**: Fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan-nxki **(Category 1)**
- **Other Recommended**: Ramucirumab monotherapy, ramucirumab + FOLFIRI/irinotecan
- **Targeted/Useful in Certain Circumstances**:
  - NTRK fusion: Entrectinib, larotrectinib, repotrectinib
  - MSI-H/dMMR: Pembrolizumab, nivo+ipi, dostarlimab
  - TMB-H: Pembrolizumab
  - BRAF V600E: Dabrafenib + trametinib
  - RET fusion: Selpercatinib

## Peritoneal Carcinoma as Only Disease (GAST-10)

- **Initial Workup**: CT, diagnostic laparoscopy with PCI staging, consider PET/EGD
- **Systemic Therapy**: Minimum 3 months → Restage
- **Low PCI (≤10), Stable/Improved, No Extraperitoneal Disease**:
  - *Complete cytoreduction predicted*: Gastrectomy + cytoreduction + IC/HIPEC or continue systemic therapy
  - *Incomplete predicted*: Clinical trial or continue systemic therapy
- **High PCI (>10), Progression, or Extraperitoneal Disease**: Systemic therapy, trial, or best supportive care
- **IC/HIPEC**: Multidisciplinary decision; PIPAC investigational only

## Follow-up & Surveillance (GAST-7)

- **H&P**: Every 3–6 mo (yrs 1–2), then 6–12 mo (yrs 3–5)
- **Early Stage (Tis/T1a post-ER)**: EGD q6mo ×1 yr, then annually ×3–5 yrs
- **Stage I (post-surgery) / Partial Gastrectomy**: EGD as clinically indicated
- **Stage II/III**: CT chest/abdomen/pelvis q6mo ×2 yrs, then annually ×5 yrs
- **Nutritional Monitoring**: Lifelong management of B12, iron, Ca, Vit D, zinc deficiencies post-gastrectomy
- **Beyond 5 Years**: Consider based on risk factors/comorbidities; routine cancer-specific surveillance not mandated

## Survivorship & Long-Term Care (GAST-I)

- **General Issues**: Weight management, diarrhea, chemotherapy-induced neuropathy (duloxetine), fatigue, bone health screening
- **Gastrectomy-Specific**:
  - Dumping syndrome (early/late), postprandial fullness, SIBO
  - Dietary modifications: Small frequent meals, avoid fluids with meals, high protein/fiber, low simple carbs
- **Supplementation**: Daily multivitamin, B12, Ca, Vit D; monitor levels regularly
- **SIBO Management**: Rifaximin + low-carb/high-protein diet
- **Care Coordination**: Clear roles between oncology & PCP, survivorship care plan, health behavior counseling

## Palliative & Best Supportive Care (GAST-J)

- **Performance Status Drives Therapy**:
  - KPS ≥60% or ECOG ≤2 → Systemic therapy/chemoradiation + BSC
  - KPS <60% or ECOG ≥3 → Best supportive care only
- **Bleeding**: Endoscopy, IR embolization, EBRT, palliative gastrectomy
- **Obstruction**: SEMS stenting, gastrojejunostomy, venting/feeding tubes, EBRT/chemotherapy
- **Pain**: EBRT, systemic therapy, NCCN pain guidelines; remove stent if severe uncontrolled pain
- **Nausea/Vomiting**: NCCN antiemesis guidelines; rule out luminal obstruction

## Summary & Key Takeaways

- Multidisciplinary management is foundational to optimal care
- Universal biomarker testing (MSI/MMR, PD-L1, HER2, CLDN18.2, NGS) standardizes treatment selection
- Early stage → Endoscopic resection or surgery; ≥T2 → Perioperative chemo ± ICI (MSI-H/dMMR)
- Postoperative therapy dictated by margin status, nodal burden, and D1/D2 dissection extent
- Advanced disease → Biomarker-driven first-line therapy; ICI + chemo standard for PD-L1+/MSI-H
- Survivorship requires proactive nutritional, metabolic, and bone health monitoring
- Early integration of palliative care improves quality of life and may extend survival
